title: Shade by the Block: Street-Tree Canopy and Afternoon Surface Heat in a Mid-Sized City
abstract: Street trees are one of the few remedies for summer heat that a city can deliver block by block. We combine a mid-afternoon thermal survey with leaf-on canopy maps for 96 blocks in the central district of Larkhaven, a mid-sized inland city, to ask how strongly canopy predicts surface temperature at the scale of a single block. Across the 90 built blocks of this illustrative dataset, each additional ten percentage points of canopy went with a surface about 1.9 °C cooler, and canopy alone accounted for 70 percent of the variation between blocks. Blocks bordering the central park were cooler than their own canopy predicts. We discuss what such a slope can and cannot tell a planting programme.
